chunks: Indeed we and our fathers had been promised this before. It is nothing but the earlier people's lore.
ai.seo_question: What did the disbelievers say about the promise of resurrection?
ai.summary: In Surah Al-An'am (specifically verse 25, though often cited in the context of the Meccan disbelievers' attitude), the polytheists of Mecca dismiss the promise of resurrection as 'legends of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin), reflecting a generational transmission of skepticism. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi in *Majma' al-Bayan*, highlight that this dismissal stems from a refusal to engage with the logical proofs of the Hereafter, relying instead on inherited tradition. This verse underscores the recurring theme of *istikbar* (arrogance) where the elite reject divine truth to maintain their worldly status.
